Bill to rename and broaden tobacco control law to cover vaporisers and psychoactive substances

Second Reading12 February 2026 – 6 March 2026 bill-intro-673, bill-785

A Bill at Second Reading, moved by Senior Minister of State for Health Dr Koh Poh Koon, to amend the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act 1993, rename it the Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act, control vaporisers and specified psychoactive substances, and provide for rehabilitation and penalties.

The Bill increases the maximum fine for purchase, use and possession of vaporisers from $2,000 to $10,000, and introduces mandatory imprisonment and higher fines for import and supply. It creates rehabilitation orders for people who consume specified psychoactive substances and for repeat vaporiser users, and places duties on owners and occupiers of specified premises and storage spaces. The Senior Minister of State said the Government intends for the Bill to commence on 1 May.

What happens next The Deputy Speaker said that if there are no clarifications arising from the Senior Minister of State's response, he will put the question to the House. The Senior Minister of State said the Government intends for the Bill to commence on 1 May.

Open questions from this debate (18)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • What considerations will determine whether a psychoactive substance is listed under the TVCA rather than the MDA?
  • What percentage reduction in youth vaping cases is targeted within 12 to 24 months?
  • Will reductions in school incidents and hospital presentations be publicly reported?
  • Will offences under this Act be treated as spent after a period?
  • What safeguards ensure laboratory accuracy for urine, hair and oral fluid testing?
  • What is the projected impact on DRC capacity?
  • Will the scope of specified premises expand beyond discotheques, pubs, bars, lounges and night clubs?
  • What is the timeline from detection to scheduling of a new psychoactive substance?
  • Will a formal review of the Part 3A framework within three to five years be conducted?
  • Will the Ministry track data of young vape users who are minors?
  • Will there be other steps to ensure recidivism amongst youth vape users remains low?
  • How will HSA be empowered to effect arrests if more harmful drugs are found during a raid for vaporisers?
  • Will other ground agencies such as LTA or Town Councils be empowered to act against vaping offences?
  • Will a national protocol for youth vaping addiction be established?
  • Will the Government adopt a tobacco cohort ban?
  • Will structured horizon scanning and digital monitoring be institutionalised?
  • Will responsible persons be required to retain offenders or is notifying authorities sufficient?
  • Will the Government set targets for complete smoking cessation?

Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill at Second Reading

Second Reading6 March 2026 bill-786

A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment, to amend the Sewerage and Drainage Act and related laws to create a coastal protection framework, including PUB powers, landowner obligations, grants and enforcement.

The Minister said sea levels may rise up to 1.15 metres by the end of this century and up to five metres with storm surges and high tides, and that around 30% of Singapore could be flooded by seawater. The Bill creates obligations for owners of Prescribed Places to put coastal protection measures in place by a stipulated date, with PUB coordinating and enforcing a continuous line of defence. It also provides for a capital grant and technical advice to support landowners.

Open questions from this debate (14)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • How will the capital grant be sized, disbursed and monitored, and when will the details be released?
  • How many affected private lessees have remaining lease terms of less than 10 years?
  • Will performance bonds or mandatory construction milestones be required for private lessees?
  • How will liability for latent defects at the interface between adjoining coastal protection measures be allocated?
  • Will PUB maintain a list of pre-approved contractors or an accreditation scheme for private-sector use?
  • How will environmental impact assessments apply to specific coastal protection works?
  • How will the Code of Practice incentivise nature-based solutions?
  • How will the $5 billion Coastal and Flood Protection Fund be prioritised and split between public and private expenditure?
  • Will an annual coastal resilience report be tabled?
  • How will flood protection manager training and certification be delivered?
  • How will the timing of site-specific studies be publicised and how can citizen scientists participate?
  • How will the Government handle a lessee that fails to complete construction before giving up the lease?
  • Will lease extensions be tied to coastal protection investments?
  • How will the public-private split in expenditure be determined?

Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Social and Family Development budget

Committee of Supply5 March 2026 – 6 March 2026 budget-2930, budget-2934

A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Social and Family Development budget, opened by Mr Xie Yao Quan moving a $100 reduction to Head I of the Estimates, with MPs raising policy asks and ministers setting out MSF plans.

The transcript sets out changes including a new $500 quarterly Partnership Payout for all ComLink+ families, a rise in the Student Care Fee Assistance income threshold from $4,500 to $6,500 benefiting around 13,000 students, and from January 2027 a higher gross monthly household income ceiling of $15,000 for childcare and Kindergarten Fee Assistance. It also states that from July 2026 subsidies for residential and community disability services will rise by up to 15 and 10 percentage points, and that filing Form 1 of an LPA will be free for citizens.

What happens next Mr Xie Yao Quan sought leave to withdraw his amendment; the Taskforce on Assurance for Families with Persons with Disabilities will release its report later this year; several measures have stated start dates, including July 2026 for disability subsidies and January 2027 for the preschool subsidy income ceiling.

Open questions from this debate (10)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether MSF will amend section 12 of the Mental Capacity Act to allow accredited organisations to serve as personal welfare donees.
  • Whether the LPA registration fee for low-wage foreign workers will be waived or reduced.
  • How the new ComLink+ milestones will be calibrated in detail.
  • Whether portable preschool subsidies will be introduced.
  • Whether a single centralised portal for PwD support will be created.
  • Whether Singapore Sign Language interpretation will be systematically funded across counselling, social support centres and crisis response services.
  • Whether a National Disability Job Redesign Fund will be established.
  • Whether domestic child abduction will get an expedited judicial pathway.
  • Whether unwed parents will receive the Baby Bonus cash gift or tax benefits.
  • Whether the right to disconnect policy for preschool educators will be formalised.
